tip: Names take siapa (who), not apa: Siapa nama kamu? is literally 'Who is your name?' – asking with apa sounds off.
The owner comes after the thing owned: keluarga kamu is literally 'family you' = your family. Reverse of English order.
Anda is the formal 'you', always capitalized, safe with strangers – kamu is for friends. Senang berkenalan dengan Anda keeps it polite.
Doubling a noun makes it plural: anak = child, anak-anak = children. No plural ending exists – repetition does the job.
